lines.text: Octopuses have three hearts. And one of them quits every time they swim.
Two of those hearts pump blood through the gills, where it picks up oxygen.
The third heart pumps it out to the rest of the body.
But when an octopus swims, that main heart stops beating.
That's why swimming wears them out, and most octopuses would rather crawl.
Oh, and their blood is blue, because it uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen.
